text: When a game is slow, measure on the target machine before cutting features: a pixel line (frame time at three render scales and a tiny window) separates pixels from the rest, and replacing one material at a time with a plain one names the dear shader. Here it showed a procedural land shader was 40 % of the frame and scripts under 1 ms, the opposite of what the cloud machine suggested.

A read-back from the GPU (viewport texture to image) stalls the main thread until the GPU has finished everything queued; baked off-screen pictures belong in a disk cache keyed by the inputs' hash, read on a worker thread, never rebuilt at each start.

With several chats on one repository, give the integration branch one fixed name that survives every handover, and have each chat keep a small status block in its own file on its own branch that a script collects into one board: renaming the lead's branch at each handover cost a round of messages and left a chat on another machine unreachable.

A test runner that loads every test script can hang silently when one script has a semantic error the syntax check does not catch: when a first run after adding a test takes far longer than expected, read the raw log before waiting.
